LESSON: COMMON ACCIDENTS EDUCATION

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES
Strand: Safety
Topic 4.1: Common accidents Education

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Common accidents Education. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What causes accidents at (8 lessons) home, electrocution, burns. home?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify ways of preventing sharp edges, slippery floors, accidents at home, vegetable/fruit peelings, broken

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: COMMON ACCIDENTS EDUCATION
Subject: HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Common accidents Education helps you succeed in HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: COMMON ACCIDENTS EDUCATION
Study Common accidents Education like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify ways of preventing sharp edges, slippery floors, accidents at home, vegetable/fruit peelings, broken

What this means
In this part you learn to identify ways of preventing sharp edges, slippery floors, accidents at home, vegetable/fruit peelings, broken. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify ways of preventing sharp edges, slippery floors, accidents at home, vegetable/fruit peelings, broken.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Common accidents Education” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify ways of preventing sharp edges, slippery floors, accidents at home, vegetable/fruit peelings, broken. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Common accidents Education is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Common accidents Education” around your school. (skill: identify ways of preventing sharp edges, slippery floors, accidents at home, vegetable/fruit peelings, broken)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Common accidents Education to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify ways of preventing sharp edges, slippery floors, accidents at home, vegetable/fruit peelings, broken.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Common accidents Education from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Common accidents Education: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 1 learner study Common accidents Education?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What causes accidents at (8 lessons) home, electrocution, burns. home?
2. How can we prevent accidents at home, causes of accidents at home such as accidents at home?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Common accidents Education means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify ways of preventing sharp edges, slippery floors, accidents at home, vegetable/fruit peelings, broken.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
